headline: There are no fixed SHS cut-off points in Ghana.
summary: The Ghana Education Service has stated publicly that placement into Senior High Schools is not decided by fixed cut-off aggregates. Any table claiming 'aggregate 6 gets you your first choice' is not official — GES has labelled such circulating tables as fake.
what_actually_decides_placement: Your raw BECE score across the six placement subjects.
How competitive the school you chose is, and how many others chose it.
Demand for the specific programme you selected, not just the school.
The order you listed your choices in on the CSSPS form.
Residency status (day or boarding) and any category restrictions on your selections.
what_category_means: Schools are grouped A to D based on their historical average performance and facilities — not on an entry threshold. A Category A school is typically more competitive because more students choose it, which indirectly means stronger aggregates tend to be placed there. But the category itself is not a cut-off you must meet.
practical_advice: Spread your choices across categories rather than picking only Category A schools.
Check that the school you choose actually offers the programme you want — many do not offer every track.
A strong student at a Category B or C school can still reach any university programme; WASSCE results are what universities look at.
Confirm details on the official CSSPS portal and GES communications rather than social media lists.

data_note: School categories in this dataset are compiled from published Category A/B/C listings and cross-checked against an internal sample. Where sources disagreed, the published listing was preferred. Categories may change between years — verify against current GES publications before making a final selection.
